I managed to fix that. Two of crash dump files located at %TEMP%\VRChat\VRChat\Crashes\ had nsi / nsi.dll and dnsapi / dnsapi.dll modules crashed with Stack overflow - code c00000fd . Possible too much redirects -> malfunctioning dns settings for whatever reason, when only vrchat was crashing. 

Running commands in CMD ( PowerShell for me ) : 

netsh int ip reset

netsh winsock reset

helped me to fix that.

So i found whats going on. with some recent updates, for whatever reason Vrchat is very not happy when you modify your winsock for ANY given reason. if you are running proxifier for example - it will interfere with Vrchat now, even if it WAS NOT THE CASE until april 4th. Dumb thing, as i run server that needs some connections to be redirected through tunnels. Now i need actually to stop server connections to run vrchat. Great.
